title: DyTwin: Federated Adaptive Digital Twins for Data Centers - Visualization and Anomaly Detection
problem: Supercomputers and data centers require reliable detection of failures and anomalies to maintain uninterrupted operation. Current systems lack adaptive mechanisms for dynamically adjusting monitoring parameters in response to changing conditions.
motivation: Anomaly detection is critical for maintaining operational reliability and preventing costly failures in modern data centers and supercomputing systems.
method: The system creates digital copies of data centers (called Digital Twins) that work together in a federated way—coordinating with each other while operating somewhat independently. It continuously monitors key metrics like power consumption and network usage, using machine learning to detect unusual patterns that signal problems. The system automatically adjusts which metrics it watches most closely based on how conditions change. Results appear in real-time on an interactive dashboard showing current state, predictions, and alerts.
key_novelty: Digital copies of data centers that coordinate with each other (federated approach) and automatically adjust what they monitor based on conditions, using machine learning to detect problems.
contributions: Federated adaptive Digital Twin framework for continuous data center monitoring
AI-powered anomaly detection with dynamic parameter tuning
Real-time visualization and forecasting dashboard for data center metrics
Experimental validation of anomaly detection effectiveness in supercomputing environments

metrics.other: Anomaly detection effectiveness and operational reliability (specific numerical metrics not provided)
